item.title: Just In: Court Resumes Trial Of Suspects Linked To Abduction Of NYSC Members, Others In Imo
item.description: Court is set to resume the trial of suspects linked to the abduction of 20 members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) and others in Imo State. The suspects were apprehended in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Abia State during intelligence-led operations conducted between October 10 and 14 by the Department of State Services (DSS), in collaboration with the military, police, and other security operatives. Three other suspects reportedly escaped with gunshot wounds, prompting a manhunt for the fleeing members of the gang. The prospective corps members were abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway in Imo State on October 1, 2026, while they were travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to their assigned NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The gunmen attacked two buses conveying the prospective corps members and other passengers near Umunoha in the Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State. The victims were rescued on October 7 during a joint security operation at Amakohia-Ubi Village in Owerri West Local Government Area of the state. They were subsequently taken to the DSS hospital in Owerri for medical attention and necessary checks. During the search-and-rescue operation, the police had said their operatives located the kidnappers’ camp through drone surveillance but could not immediately advance because the location was reportedly planted with improvised explosive devices (IEDs). Security agencies later intensified efforts to reach the victims and secure their release. item.title: Ebola: Medical laboratory scientists urge virtual campaigns ahead of 2027 elections
item.description: The Association of Medical Laboratory Scientists of Nigeria (AMLSN), Kaduna State Branch, has advised political parties to campaign virtually to minimise physical contact amid the Ebola outbreak. Mr Turman Benjamin, Chairman of the association in Kaduna gave the advice on Thursday in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Kaduna. Benjamin recommended social media, text messages, telephone calls and virtual meeting platforms such as Zoom and Google Meet as alternatives to physical political rallies. He said the approach would reduce unnecessary contact and help minimise potential exposure while health authorities worked to contain the outbreak. Benjamin urged the Kaduna State Government to intensify public awareness, trace any contacts linked to the confirmed case and ensure adequate protective equipment for healthcare workers. He advised residents to avoid unnecessary physical contact, including handshakes and hugs, and observe appropriate hygiene measures. The medical laboratory scientist said Ebola could be transmitted through direct contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of infected persons. He also urged the public to avoid handling the bodies of suspected or confirmed Ebola victims without appropriate training and protective equipment. Benjamin said only trained and properly equipped personnel should handle such bodies to reduce the risk of infection during burial preparations. He called on the government to provide hospitals with adequate personal protective equipment, including gloves and other appropriate protective gear. According to him, laboratory testing is essential to confirm Ebola because its early symptoms can resemble those of other illnesses, including malaria and typhoid fever. Benjamin further advised the public to exercise caution when handling or consuming wild animals that could carry infectious diseases. He urged the media to intensify public education on Ebola transmission, prevention and the importance of seeking prompt medical attention when symptoms develop. The chairman also called for vigilance among healthcare workers and members of the public, stressing the importance of early detection and effective infection prevention measures. The NAN reports that the Federal Government has confirmed one case of Ebola disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, with 44 close contacts identified for monitoring to prevent further transmission. The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received treatment for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed. The woman has since been placed in isolation and is receiving medical care, while health authorities have commenced contact tracing to identify and monitor people who may have been exposed to the virus.( NAN ) The post Ebola: Medical laboratory scientists urge virtual campaigns ahead of 2027 elections appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: No vaccine, specific treatment for Ebola strain in Nigeria – WHO
item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with the World Health Organization (WHO) saying there is no vaccine or specific treatment for the index Ebola virus case detected in Nigeria, which carried the Bundibugyo strain. Another headline features the Senate Committee on Public Accounts rejecting the volume of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) imports reported by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) for 2022 and 2023 over significant discrepancies with figures supplied by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL). Vanguard also reports that the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, said only 108 out of about 39,000 underage candidates who sat the 2026 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME) have survived the Federal Government’s rigorous screening for possible admission into tertiary institutions. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian’s lead headline states that weak oversight and fiscal plan have left over 6,000 projects abandoned across the country, with their combined value running into trillions of naira. The Punch reports that the diplomat diagnosed with the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, has reportedly deteriorated into multi-organ failure, as the Federal Government and state governments intensify surveillance, contact tracing and emergency preparedness to prevent the spread of the deadly disease. Lastly, The Nation reports that Vice President Kashim Shettima challenged state governments to stop depending on the Federal Government for solutions to their electricity challenges. item.title: Troops rescue four kidnapped victims in Zamfara, Kebbi
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Sector 2, Operation Fansan Yamma, have rescued four kidnapped victims during separate intelligence-led operations in Zamfara and Kebbi states as the military intensifies efforts to combat terrorism and kidnapping across the North West. According to the Army, the victims were rescued on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, in Maru Local Government Area of Zamfara State and between Bena and Sawade in Kebbi State. “In Zamfara, troops rescued Mansur Shehu, 25, and Kadijat Haruna, 49, following a response to a reported terrorist incident on farmland across a river in Binoni Marafa, Maru LGA. “In Kebbi, troops conducted a search-and-rescue operation after receiving reports of suspected terrorists moving with kidnapped victims from Dupindu Village, Kanya District, Danko-Wasagu LGA. “The operation secured the freedom of Jimoh Su-Arege, 35, and Kalahe Danjuma, 41, who were subsequently handed over to the Seriki of Dipindu. “The military said troops have continued to intensify patrols and surveillance across affected communities to strengthen security, dominate operational areas and deny criminal elements freedom of action. “The successful operations highlight Operation Fansan Yamma’s sustained efforts to rescue abducted persons, disrupt terrorist activities and restore peace across Zamfara and Kebbi states,” the military said. item.title: Ogun shuts schools as over 100 pupils are hospitalised after gas emissions
item.description: By James Ogunnaike Abeokuta The Ogun State government has ordered the closure of some schools in Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye and Ijebu-Igbo following the hospitalisation of more than 100 pupils on Wednesday after suspected exposure to an offensive gaseous substance. The affected pupils were rushed to the State Hospital, Ijebu-Ode; the General Hospital, Ijebu-Igbo; and other healthcare facilities for medical attention. Among the schools worst affected were Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School, Anglican Girls Grammar School, Ijebu-Ode, Itamerin Comprehensive High School and some schools in Ago-Iwoye. A video circulating on social media showed pupils reportedly fainting and being rushed to hospitals following the incident. The state government had previously identified the substance as methane, although the precise source of the recurring emissions remains under investigation. A teacher at one of the affected schools, who spoke to our correspondent on condition of anonymity, said the incident occurred at about 10am when pupils and staff began experiencing breathing difficulties, with some collapsing. “The pupils and staff started inhaling the gas and began to have difficulty breathing. Some of them fainted and were rushed to hospitals,” the teacher said. Bello said the situation was under control, assuring residents that the government would work towards finding a lasting solution to the recurring problem. He said the government’s investigations had indicated that the phenomenon was a natural occurrence associated with geological and tectonic fault lines, rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak. Bello urged residents to remain calm, adding that the affected pupils were expected to recover after receiving medical attention. He also advised residents exposed to the odour to cover their noses and mouths with wet handkerchiefs rather than wear nose masks. As of the time of filing this report, medical personnel were attending to affected pupils at various hospitals. item.title: NEMA Distributes Relief Materials To Gas Seepage-Affected Persons In Rivers Community
item.description: The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) has distributed relief materials to persons affected by gas seepage in Bille Community, Degema Local Government Area of Rivers State. The intervention, carried out through NEMA’s Port Harcourt Operations Office, is aimed at easing the immediate humanitarian needs of residents affected by the incident. The exercise began with a courtesy visit to the King of Bille Kingdom, His Royal Majesty, King Igbikingeri Ngowari Cornelius. The delegation, representing the NEMA Director-General, Hajiya Umar, was led by Chidi Ogundu, who conveyed the agency’s message of sympathy to the monarch and the people of Bille Kingdom. The delegation later proceeded to Bille Community, where the relief materials were presented to community executives and leaders for distribution to affected persons. The exercise was conducted with measures in place to ensure an orderly and effective delivery of the assistance. Representatives of the Rivers State Emergency Management Agency (RISEMA) and the Nigerian Red Cross Society, alongside other stakeholders, witnessed the distribution. Community leaders expressed appreciation to NEMA and its Director-General for the intervention, saying the relief materials would help ease the hardship faced by residents. They also called for medical outreaches to help identify and address potential health problems associated with prolonged exposure to gas. The gas seepage, which began more than three months ago, is yet to receive a concrete solution from the Federal Government. Investigations into the incident are reportedly ongoing, involving the Federal Ministry of Gas, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), partners and operators. Residents continue to await a lasting solution to the problem and measures to address the potential health risks posed by prolonged exposure to the gas. item.title: Iran’s Guards threaten to hit US bases in retaliation for Hormuz escorts
item.description: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. “The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement on their Sepah News website. “This is a serious warning,” they added. Iran claims control over Hormuz, a strategic shipping route through which one-fifth of the world’s oil supplies passed before war broke out in February. It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation. item.title: Sowore claps back after Senator Ajibola called him ‘skit maker’
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, has hit back at the National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ajibola Basiru, after the senator described him as a “skit maker” and “comedian”. Sowore, in a statement posted on X, recalled his longstanding relationship with Basiru, saying they fought against military dictatorship together in the 1990s. He also accused the APC chieftain of abandoning the democratic ideals they once defended because of the privileges of his current political position. The exchange followed Basiru’s appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, where he described Sowore as a skit maker. Responding, Sowore shared a photograph of himself with Basiru taken in 1998, when he led the Congress of Progressive Youths (COPY), a pro-democracy group. “I watched an interview on Politics Today on Channels Television, anchored by Seun Okinbaloye, in which the APC National Secretary, Ajibola Basiru, called me a ‘skit maker’ and ‘comedian’,” he wrote. Sowore said he received Basiru at the University of Lagos after the latter was expelled from the University of Ilorin in 1992 over student activism. He said he and other activists, including Kunle Adegoke, popularly known as K-Rad, helped Basiru secure an opportunity to return to the university and study law. “Both eventually graduated with flying colours and went on to accomplish great things,” Sowore said, adding that their shared history made Basiru’s remarks particularly disappointing. He argued that the struggle for democracy and human dignity should not be dismissed as entertainment, insisting that his activism remained consistent with the ideals they defended during military rule. “The struggle for justice, democracy, freedom and the preservation of human dignity is neither skit-making nor comedy,” he said. Sowore also faulted Basiru’s argument that opposition candidates should be ashamed of losing to President Bola Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, which he described as deeply flawed. He maintained that political appointments were temporary and predicted that Tinubu’s administration, like previous military regimes, would eventually leave office. “Political appointments are temporary. Tinubu’s regime will come and go, just like the military regimes we confronted in our youth,” he said. Sowore concluded by accusing Basiru of turning against the ideals he once championed. “What is truly comical is watching yesterday’s beneficiaries of resistance become today’s defenders of the very oppression they once fought against,” he wrote. item.title: Ekiti Assembly passes State Police Bill
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela The Ekiti State House of Assembly has passed the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, seeking to provide for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. The bill scaled second and third readings during plenary on Tuesday, with all 21 members present voting in support, signalling the Assembly’s endorsement of decentralised policing. Following its passage, the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Adeoye Stephen Aribasoye, directed the Clerk of the House to transmit the document to the National Assembly alongside observations made by the state legislature. Speaking on the bill, Aribasoye said state police had remained at the forefront of national discourse for over two decades, noting that the Ekiti Assembly had a historic opportunity to take a position. He stressed the need for effective and responsive security, saying Nigeria’s policing challenges required practical solutions. “Nigerians had repeatedly expressed concerns over delayed responses to distress calls, limitations in operational reach and the distance between law enforcement agencies and the communities they were meant to protect,” he said. The Speaker added that inadequate and poorly coordinated local policing in some areas had contributed to insecurity, threatening livelihoods, disrupting education, undermining business confidence and eroding public trust. He said a properly structured State Police system could strengthen accountability by bringing policing leadership and oversight closer to the people and their elected representatives, subject to constitutional safeguards. According to him, the country could not afford unnecessary delays in addressing security challenges, describing State Police as “a long-overdue practical necessity rather than a mere theoretical preference.” In its report, the Committee of the Whole House recommended concurrence to the bill, subject to an amendment to Section 317A(5). The committee said it considered the bill clause by clause and deliberated on the proposed constitutional framework for the establishment and operation of State Police Services. It proposed the insertion of the words “an Act of the National Assembly or a Law of the State House of Assembly, as applicable” after the words “this Constitution” in the newly inserted Section 317A(5). The observation, the committee noted, is intended to expressly recognise the legislative authority of the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly, within their respective constitutional jurisdictions, in authorising relevant security arrangements. item.title: Libya recovers Swiss, Austrian women kidnapped since 2025 in Niger
item.description: Two women — one Swiss and the other Austrian — were released from more than a year of captivity in Niger and arrived in Libya’s eastern city of Benghazi, Libyan media outlets reported on Thursday. The two women — Swiss national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Austrian Claudia Abbt, 69 — were abducted in Niger in 2025. In a video released by Libya’s eastern-based al-Masar TV, the women appeared emaciated and thanked the country’s eastern-based military commander Khalifa Haftar and his son, Saddam, for their release. Al-Masar said “two hostages, an Austrian and a Swiss national, have been freed after being held captive in Niger for a year and a half”. “My name is Eva Gretzmacher, I am 76, and I thank from the bottom of my heart Marshal Haftar and his son, Saddam, who released us,” one of the woman said in French. “I had been held hostage for a year and nine months,” she said. Abbt said she was “happy to be free”, also thanking Haftar. Online website Libyan News Observatory also reported their release. Libya has struggled to recover from the chaos that followed the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi. Two governments are currently vying for power: a UN-recognised administration in Tripoli led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah and its rival in the east backed by Haftar. item.title: Websites down: what is PHP and how has it raised AI hacking fears?
item.description: Artificial intelligence has found critical security flaws in a major programming language called PHP, with many websites taken offline Thursday as organisations worldwide scramble to fend off would-be hackers. Created in the early 1990s, PHP is a computer programming language that helps run an estimated 70 percent of the world’s websites. It is “a backbone of the web”, according to security firm Wiz Research, which says it used AI to find vulnerabilities hidden in PHP for more than a decade. PHP — a name that originally stood for Personal Home Page — underpins popular web design platforms, meaning the flaws could allow hackers to break into various sites, from online stores to government services. A fix was released Wednesday, with the PHP Foundation telling the tech departments of companies and organisations around the world: “If you run PHP, it is imperative that you update now.” That has resulted in a slew of apps and websites — from the Paris police website to a Pokemon sleep tracker — going dark as developers work to protect their underlying code from hacks. How did AI find the flaws? Cutting-edge AI models, such as those from US giants OpenAI and Google, were used by Wiz and other groups to uncover PHP’s weak spots in August. This was kept under wraps while a fix was developed. item.description: The United Nations has expressed confidence in Nigeria’s capacity to contain its newly confirmed Ebola case, pledging support to prevent further spread of the deadly disease. UN Secretary-General’s Spokesperson, Stéphane Dujarric, gave the assurance on Wednesday while responding to questions from the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) at the UN Headquarters in New York. Dujarric said the UN was concerned about the detection of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus in Nigeria, the fifth country to report a case during the current outbreak. However, he expressed confidence in Nigeria’s health authorities, commending their swift response and extensive contact-tracing efforts following the confirmation. “We have full confidence in the ability and the capacity of the Nigerian Government’s health authorities to deal with this single case,” he said. The spokesperson acknowledged that the appearance of the virus in another country raised concerns about its potential spread beyond countries already affected. “Yeah, I mean, it’s of course concerning that there is a case in a new country,” Dujarric said. He, however, noted that Nigerian authorities had already undertaken active contact tracing to identify and monitor people potentially exposed to the infected patient. Asked by NAN whether the UN was worried that the outbreak could spread to additional countries or persist for another year, Dujarric emphasised international cooperation. item.title: Kano will vote Tinubu in 2027, Yusuf assures
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf has assured President Bola Tinubu of the support of Kano residents in the 2027 general election, expressing confidence that they will vote for the President to ensure the continuation of his development projects. Yusuf spoke on Wednesday while representing Tinubu at the commissioning of a section of the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Highway at Tamburawa, Kano State. He praised the President for projects being executed by the Federal Government, saying the highway would ease transportation across Northern Nigeria. The governor also said several projects executed by the Tinubu administration had not received adequate publicity. “I have seen many projects the President has executed that have not been publicised. I could go on and on listing the projects and initiatives of this administration,” Yusuf said. He expressed confidence that residents of Kano and other parts of the country would support Tinubu in the next general election. “The people of Kano will come out en masse to vote for President Tinubu, not only in Kano but across the North-West, the South and the country at large, to ensure the continuation of his development projects,” he added. Umahi Says Economic Hardship Easing Also speaking at the event, the Minister of Works, David Umahi, said the worst of Nigeria’s economic hardship was over, insisting that the Tinubu administration’s reforms were beginning to yield positive results. “The reforms have started to yield dividends of democracy. Even in the darkest hour before dawn, there is hope. Let us support President Bola Tinubu,” Umahi said. He cited road projects in Kano and other parts of the North-West as evidence of the administration’s efforts, adding that the Federal Government was working to complete projects inherited from the late President Muhammadu Buhari. “There is no project started by the late President Buhari that President Bola Tinubu is not doing in the North,” he said. Umahi listed several road projects in the region, including the Kano Northern Bypass, Kano Ring Road, Kano-Kongolam road and Zaria-Hunkuyi road projects. He also said the Federal Government was working on the Sokoto-Zamfara-Zaria road. According to the minister, some inherited projects have been redesigned to feature reinforced concrete pavement. Umahi said the Tinubu administration had completed close to 400 kilometres of roads in the North-West within three years, while about 4,000 kilometres of road projects were ongoing in the region. He added that the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Highway would benefit not only the North-West but also other parts of the country. item.title: Delta traditional rulers mourn Uduaghan
item.description: The Delta State Council of Traditional Rulers has mourned former Governor Emmanuel Ewetan Uduaghan, describing him as a detribalised leader whose legacy of peace, development and support for traditional institutions would endure. The council, in a condolence message dated October 21, 2026, extended its sympathies to the Uduaghan family of Abigborodo, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the people of Delta State over the former governor’s death. The message was signed by the Chairman of the council, the Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, HRM Orhue I, CFR, MNI. The traditional rulers said the news of Uduaghan’s death was received with shock and profound bewilderment, recalling his cordial relationship with the traditional institution during his tenure as governor. According to the council, Uduaghan prioritised the welfare of traditional rulers and made significant contributions to human capital development, infrastructure and the promotion of peace among the state’s ethnic groups. It described the former governor as a detribalised leader who treated all parts of Delta as one indivisible family, irrespective of ethnic differences. The council noted that although Uduaghan inherited the Warri crisis from his predecessor, he worked to establish lasting peace among the three warring ethnic groups. It said his contributions would continue to resonate among Deltans, particularly his efforts to strengthen the traditional institution and enhance its standing alongside similar institutions in other states. The council prayed for the repose of Uduaghan’s soul and other departed faithful, while asking God to comfort his immediate family, the Delta State Government and the people of the state over what it described as an irreparable loss. item.title: Yobe court sentences man to death for killing wife
item.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman A Yobe State High Court sitting in Damaturu has sentenced a 45-year-old man, Abubakar Musa, popularly known as Daddy, to death by hanging for the killing of his wife, Ammi Adamu Mamman. Musa was arrested on January 4, 2024, following his wife’s death at New Bra-Bra Estate, Damaturu, and was subsequently charged with culpable homicide, according to media reports. The then Police Public Relations Officer of the Yobe State Command, DSP Dungus Abdulkarim, said the incident occurred at about 4:48 a.m. on January 4, after the ‘C’ Divisional Police Headquarters in Damaturu received a distress call. Abdulkarim said the couple were on the same bed when Mamman was allegedly attacked with a sharp object on the neck, causing severe bleeding that led to her death. He said Musa was arrested for interrogation, while the homicide unit of the State Criminal Investigation Department commenced an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident. The case subsequently went to High Court 1 in Damaturu, where the judge reportedly held that the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. University Community Mourned Deceased Mamman’s death also drew reactions from the university community. A February 2024 newsletter published by Yobe State University identified her as a member of staff and said the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Mala Mohammed Daura, mourned her death and called on security agencies to ensure that those responsible were brought to justice. The university described her death as a loss to its community. She was buried in Potiskum on January 9, 2024, according to the newsletter. The Women-led Civil Society Organizations Network in Yobe State also condemned the killing and called for justice. In a statement issued shortly after the incident, the network identified the deceased as Ammi Adamu Mamman and said she was a volunteer with one of its member organisations. Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, also expressed condolences to the family and called on security agencies to establish the circumstances surrounding her death, assuring that anyone found responsible would face the law. A lawyer quoted in media reports said Musa retained the right to appeal the judgment within the period prescribed by law. The Group is also developing a major petroleum distribution corridor linking Djibouti and Addis Ababa, complete with storage terminals and tank farms designed to facilitate the efficient transportation and storage of refined products. He added that another strategic project in Cameroon is nearing completion, while Namibia has been identified as a critical hub in the Group’s plan to penetrate Southern African markets. Dangote described Namibia as a particularly attractive location because of its strategic proximity to the Dangote Petroleum Refinery in Lagos. “From our refinery to Namibia is just about four days of steaming,” he noted. According to him, refined products from the Lagos refinery will be transported to Namibia and distributed across interconnected markets, including Botswana and South Africa. The Group is also examining other supply corridors extending into Zimbabwe and Zambia as part of its broader objective of developing a continental network supported by strategically located storage and transportation infrastructure. The petroleum distribution expansion complements plans to establish another refinery in Lamu, Kenya, with a projected refining capacity of approximately 700,000 barrels per day. Dangote noted that East Africa’s growing economies, vibrant mining sector and increasing energy demand make the region an attractive destination for refining investments. He explained that the proposed refinery would source crude oil from multiple markets rather than depend exclusively on supplies from Kenya or Uganda, ensuring greater flexibility and long-term operational sustainability. According to him, technical assessments identified Lamu as the preferred location because of its deep-water access, marine infrastructure and availability of critical resources required for large-scale refining operations. Dangote revealed that the investment decision was concluded within four months, although he alleged that vested commercial interests attempted to delay the project through legal proceedings shortly before its public announcement. He questioned why African countries should be discouraged from supporting local industries when developed economies increasingly deploy similar measures to strengthen domestic manufacturing and employment. Drawing parallels with recent developments in major global economies, he argued that industrial protection remains a legitimate and widely accepted economic strategy. “If America is now saying, no, we are going to protect our industries, who are we in Africa not to protect our own industries?” he asked. Dangote also disclosed that the Group has earmarked approximately $50 billion for investments between 2026 and 2030, describing the programme as part of a broader mission to demonstrate that African businesses can successfully execute transformative industrial projects at scale. “The legacy we are trying to set up is how do we industrialise our continent?” he said. According to him, the investment programme is designed not only to expand the Group’s operations but also to inspire other African entrepreneurs and investors to pursue ambitious industrial ventures capable of reshaping the continent’s economic future. Looking beyond the energy sector, Dangote identified inadequate power supply, weak financial systems and underdeveloped industrial policies as major challenges constraining Africa’s economic growth. He described electricity as a fundamental requirement for industrialisation, particularly in manufacturing, mining and mineral processing, where reliable power is essential for value addition. With an estimated 650 million Africans still lacking access to electricity, he stressed that addressing the continent’s energy deficit would unlock significant opportunities for job creation, industrial development and economic diversification. Questioning why a continent blessed with abundant natural resources, vast arable land and a young population continues to grapple with poverty, Dangote insisted that Africa possesses all the ingredients necessary to become a major industrial powerhouse. item.description: A lawyer for Leopoldo Luque, a doctor charged in the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona, said in closing arguments Wednesday that his client was innocent and had been made a “scapegoat.” Attorney Roberto Rallin rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s November 2020 death was foreseeable, while another defense attorney, Francisco Oneto, maintained that his death resulted from an “acute and unpredictable” heart attack. “There was absolutely no possibility of predicting this fatal outcome,” Oneto insisted. Prosecutors have requested a 12-year prison sentence for Luque, a neurosurgeon considered a key decision-maker for Maradona at the time of his death. “We are here to proclaim Luque’s innocence, not with television slogans, but with the evidence that supports it,” Rallin said. “Leopoldo Luque has been the scapegoat.” Maradona died at age 60 from a cardiorespiratory crisis coupled with pulmonary edema. He was found dead in his bed at a residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence, following surgery for a subdural hematoma. The death of Argentina’s favorite son plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic. Tens of thousands of people defied social distancing rules to bid farewell to him as he lay in state at the presidential palace. A total of seven health-care professionals have been on trial since April for potential negligence leading to the star’s death during his two weeks of convalescence. item.title: “It’s not debatable, we can’t go back,” Mbah backs Tinubu on fuel subsidy removal
item.description: …Says “We’ve delivered good governance to Enugu” Governor of Enug State, Dr. Peter Mbah, has doubled down in his support for the removal of fuel subsidy by President Bola Tinubu’s administration, saying it was undebatable and inconceivable for anyone to imagine a return to the old order. Mbah spoke at the “Meet the Candidates” town hall meeting organised by Afia TV in Enugu on Wednesday, where he also said that his administration had delivered good governance to the people of the state across all sectors. He described it as a pathetic misconception of the country’s situation and the direction it was headed for anyone to talk about the reintroduction of fuel subsidy. “If you reintroduce fuel subsidy today, we will lose ten times whatever we are currently trying to gain in terms of the removal of subsidy. The poverty rate that you are going to experience will be very high because the naira would be automatically devalued. “We cannot go back to subsidy. And I do not think it is in the interest of the country for us to even debate that. “Again, we should not even debate it because we do not want to send a signal to prospective investors that we are contemplating it. So, it is not even a subject to debate. It is something that we have moved on from, and we should be thinking about how to ensure that the natural benefits cascade to the households, create jobs and generate wealth for our people,” he said. item.title: Amnesty Int’l demands release of journalist jailed over comments on police
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Amnesty International has demanded the immediate release of 23-year-old journalist Farida Isiak, who was sentenced to four years in prison or a fine of N1.75 million over a Facebook post criticising the police in Kaduna State. The human rights organisation said her arrest and punishment “were clearly because of her attempt to expose abuses by the police.” “Sentencing a journalist to 4-years in prison after a sham trial is a travesty of justice,” it said. Isiak, a reporter with Nagarta Radio in Kaduna, was reportedly taken into custody around 10pm on October 20 by officers under the command of the Divisional Police Officer of Mararaban Jos, Usman Adamu. According to the global rights group, the case began as a minor disagreement between her mother and a neighbour over N100 change during a sale of charcoal. Police first arrested her mother, then detained her father when he went to secure her release, “using their detention as leverage to force Farida to come to the police station.” At the station, officers accused her of defaming them over a Facebook post in which she criticised their unlawful treatment of her parents. Following pressure by the police, she deleted the post and apologised, hoping it would secure her parents’ release. The officers instead kept her in custody and took her to a Sharia Court in Kawo. The presiding judge sentenced her to four years in prison or a fine of N1.75 million for defamation, “completely ignoring the initial police misconduct and the abusive actions that led to the incident.” Amnesty International said: “The arrest, detention, and hasty sentencing of Farida Isiak are a flagrant abuse of power by the police and weaponization of the judicial system to silence free speech and intimidate journalists.” It added that “arresting and holding a citizen’s parents to force a journalist to hand herself over is an unlawful tactic that violates rule of law. Demanding accountability for police actions is a constitutional right”. It called on the Kaduna State Police Command and Nigerian judicial authorities to “immediately release Farida Isiak, drop all charges, and cancel the fine imposed on her.” The organisation also urged the Nigeria Police Force to launch a full and independent investigation into the conduct of the officers involved in the unlawful detention of her family. “Nigerian authorities must stop using defamation charges and the legal system to harass journalists and restrict press freedom,” it said. item.title: Maradona’s Doctor Was Made ‘Scapegoat’ For His Death, Lawyer Tells Court
item.description: A lawyer for Leopoldo Luque, a doctor charged in the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona, said in closing arguments Wednesday that his client was innocent and had been made a “scapegoat.” Attorney Roberto Rallin rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s November 2020 death was foreseeable, while another defense attorney, Francisco Oneto, maintained that his death resulted from an “acute and unpredictable” heart attack. “There was absolutely no possibility of predicting this fatal outcome,” Oneto insisted. Prosecutors have requested a 12-year prison sentence for Luque, a neurosurgeon considered a key decision-maker for Maradona at the time of his death. “We are here to proclaim Luque’s innocence, not with television slogans, but with the evidence that supports it,” Rallin said. “Leopoldo Luque has been the scapegoat.” Maradona died at age 60 from a cardiorespiratory crisis coupled with pulmonary edema. He was found dead in his bed at a residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence, following surgery for a subdural hematoma. The death of Argentina’s favorite son plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic. Tens of thousands of people defied social distancing rules to bid farewell to him as he lay in state at the presidential palace. A total of seven health-care professionals have been on trial since April for potential negligence leading to the star’s death during his two weeks of convalescence. The presentation took place at the Oba’s Palace in Benin City as part of activities marking the traditional ruler’s 10th coronation anniversary. Meanwhile, as part of activities marking his 10th year coronation anniversary, the Oba of Benin has promised to re-establish ties with Portugal, which was the first European country to come into the kingdom. Chairman of the 10th Coronation Anniversary Committee and former Deputy Governor of Edo State, Chief Lucky Imasue, said The Netherlands had initiated the return of artefacts taken from Benin following the 1897 invasion. Imasue said every Benin artefact belonged to the Oba of Benin, regardless of the quantity, adding that more artefacts were expected to be returned. He said the artefact was presented by the Consul General of the Netherlands, Mr. Frank Keurnorst, alongside Beatrice van Bormann, Executive Director of Museum De Fundatie, in the Netherlands. He described the return on October 20, as significant, coming exactly 10 years after Ewuare’s coronation and 129 years after many historical objects were looted from the Benin Kingdom. Imasue recalled that the artefacts documented the majesty of the Oba and life in the kingdom, describing them as historical records kept in the palace before the invasion. “Efforts to recover the artefacts date back to previous Obas, but gained momentum under Ewuare, whose diplomatic experience as a former ambassador helped advance the campaign,” he said. item.title: Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes criticised manager Michael Carrick’s tactics following the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. United fell behind to a second-minute goal and never recovered as the club’s winless run reached seven games after another lacklustre performance. “We started on the wrong foot and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.” The Portugal midfielder suggested Nico Paz’s early strike for Como on Wednesday night had a damaging effect on the visitors, leaving them struggling to impose themselves. Paz scored again after Tasos Douvikas had doubled the lead, with Jacobo Ramon adding a fourth. Only a stoppage-time goal from Joshua Zirkzee stopped United from succumbing to their joint-heaviest Champions League loss. “Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood of defeat,” said Fernandes. “It’s difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. “If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.” Fernandes also highlighted United’s passive approach out of possession, saying Como were allowed too much time and space to dictate play. Asked whether those comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes said: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me. “Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Fernandes is the latest United player to publicly break ranks. Defender Lisandro Martinez took aim at the club’s hierarchy following a 2-0 Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid last week. Martinez said Carrick had been left with an understrength squad. He later apologised. Youri Tielemans, who started alongside Fernandes in the United midfield in Italy, admitted the display was simply not good enough. “We got outplayed for most of the game so it was a very disappointing night,” said Tielemans. “You can be good tactically but if the effort is not good (then it will not work) and vice versa. You need to be good at everything and tonight we were poor.” AFP The post Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .
